title: PRAY THIS AND SOMEONE WILL BLESS YOU OUT OF NOWHERE
text: Wait. Wait. Wait. Do not touch that phone. Do not scroll past The Holy Ghost arrested me in my prayer closet this morning. He seized me and he said, "The person who is about to listen to this prayer does not know what is coming. They do not know what I have set in motion. They do not know who I am about to send. They do not know what door I am about to open. But by the end of this prayer, the wheels of heaven will be turning and someone someone they did not plan for, someone they did not expect, someone they did not even know existed is going to bless them out of nowhere." That is what the Holy Ghost said to me. And if you are hearing this, it is not by accident. You were supposed to be here. This moment was divinely orchestrated. God woke you up this morning, put this in your feed, directed your algorithm, prompted your friend to send the link. Whatever happened, it was God engineering this encounter because what he wants to release through this prayer is not general. It is specific and it has your name on it. Now, quickly before we go further, I need you to be an instrument of this blessing. Share this right now. Send it to five people, 10 people, 20 people. Share it on every platform you have because the blessing that comes through distribution is different from the blessing that comes through consumption. When you become the channel through which God's word reaches others, you position yourself as a conduit and conduits are never empty. The pipeline that carries water to others is always wet. Share it now. Somebody's miracle is locked inside your obedience to share. Now, I want to worship, but not the way you expect. I do not want to sing a worship song right away. I want to start with gratitude. Raw, unscripted gratitude. Because the atmosphere for unexpected blessing is cultivated through Thanksgiving. Lift your hands wherever you are and begin to thank God not for what he is about to do, for what he has already done. Thank him for waking you up this morning. Some people went to sleep last night and their bodies are in the mortuary this morning, but you are alive. Thank him. Thank him for breath. Thank him for sanity. Thank him for the roof over your head. Thank him for the food you ate, even if it was small. Thank him for the phone or device you are using to hear this word. Thank him for the strength in your bones. Thank him for another chance. Just say, "Thank you, Father. Thank you, Lord. Thank you, Jesus. I do not deserve it, but you gave it. I did not earn it, but you provided it. Your mercies are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness." Lamentations chapter 3, verses 22 to 23. Now, let us sing. Let us worship the king. Great is thy faithfulness. Oh God, my Father, there is no shadow of turning with thee. Thou changest not. Thy compassions, they fail not. As thou hast been, thou forever will be. Great is thy faithfulness. Great is thy faithfulness. Morning by morning, new mercies I see. And all I have needed, thy hand hath provided. Great is thy faithfulness. Lord, unto me. One more time. And this time, do not just sing it, mean it. Let the words come from the basement of your soul. Let worship drip from the walls of your spirit. Let thanksgiving saturate the atmosphere around you until angels begin to lean in and listen. Great is thy faithfulness. Oh God, my father. There is no shadow of turning with thee. Thou changes not. Thy compassions, they fail not. As thou has been, thou forever will be. Great is thy faithfulness. Great is thy faithfulness. Morning by morning new mercies I see. All I have needed, thy hand hath provided. Great is thy faithfulness, [music] Lord unto me. Oh father, we worship you. We bow at your feet. We lay our crowns before your throne. You are the God who provides before we ask. You are the God who answers before we call. Isaiah chapter 65 verse 24, and it shall come to pass that before they call, I will answer, and while they are yet speaking, I will hear. That is the kind of God you are. You do not wait for us to finish praying before you move. You are already moving. You were moving before this service started. You were arranging things before we opened our mouths, and we worship you for that. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Now, let worship shift. Let us go deeper. There is none holy as the Lord. There is none beside thee. Neither is there any rock like our God. There is none holy as the Lord. There is none holy as the Lord. There is none beside thee. Neither is there any rock like our God. There is none holy as the Lord. First Samuel chapter 2 verse 2. That is Hannah's song. The woman who was barren, the woman who was mocked, the woman who was provoked year after year, but God remembered her. And when God remembered her, everything changed. She conceived, she bought a son, she named him Samuel, asked of God, and her testimony outlived her pain. I prophesy over you right now, God is remembering you in this service, at this moment. He's remembering your prayers, he's remembering your tears, he's remembering your faithfulness. He's remembering your seed, and what he remembers he rewards. What he recalls he responds to. Your season of being forgotten is ending. Your days of being overlooked are concluding. Someone is about to remember you, and that remembrance will come with a blessing you did not see coming. Hallelujah. Sit down in the spirit. Sit. But let every antenna in your spirit be fully extended, because what I am about to teach is going to unlock a dimension of provision that most believers have never accessed. Now, go with me to 2 Kings chapter 4, verses 8 through 10. I want you to see something powerful here. The Bible says, "And it fell on a day that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman, and she constrained him to eat bread. And so it was that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread. And she said unto her husband, 'Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually. Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall, and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick, and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.'" Now, watch this. This is a woman who blessed a man of God. She did not know him well. She perceived something. She discerned something. She recognized something about him, and she blessed him. She blessed him with hospitality. She blessed him with provision. She blessed him with comfort. But notice, Elisha did not ask for it. He did not send a request letter. He did not post a GoFundMe. He did not hint. He did not manipulate. The blessing came unsolicited. >> [music] >> It came from nowhere. A woman he barely knew decided to become his blessing. Why? Because God put it in her heart. And this is a principle I want you to understand this morning. God has the ability and he exercises it regularly to put it in someone's heart to bless you. He can touch the mind of a stranger. He can stir the emotions of a colleague. He can move the hand of a boss. He can redirect the generosity of a wealthy person. He can influence the decision of a committee. He can orchestrate a conversation in a boardroom where your name comes up and somebody says, "Let us bless this person." Proverbs chapter 21 verse 1. The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord. As the rivers of water, he turneth it whithersoever he will. If God can turn the heart of a king, he can turn the heart of anyone. Your landlord, your employer, your client, your professor, your in-law, your neighbor. The person sitting next to you on the bus, the person standing behind you in the queue. God can touch any heart at any time and make them become an instrument of unexpected blessing in your life. That is what we are praying into this morning. We are not just praying general prayers. We are specifically asking God to activate hearts. We are asking him to stir spirits. We are asking him to put it in somebody's mind today to bless you out of nowhere. Now go with me to another scripture. Genesis chapter 26 verses 12 to 14. Then Isaac sowed in that land and received in the same year an hundredfold and the Lord blessed him. And the man waxed great and went forward and grew until he became [clears throat] very great. For he had possession of flocks and possession of herds and great store of servants and the Philistines envied him. Isaac sowed in a land of farming. The economy was bad. The conditions were hostile. There was drought. There was scarcity. There was lack everywhere, but Isaac sowed. [music] And in the same year, not the next decade, not after many years, in the same year he received a hundredfold return and he grew until he became very great. So great that the Philistines who were the natives of that land, the established people, the ones who had been there before Isaac envied him. Now here is the revelation. The blessing on Isaac's life was so powerful that it attracted provision from the very environment that was supposed to limit him. The farming that destroyed others enriched him. The drought that impoverished his neighbors made him prosper. The scarcity that bankrupted the Philistines made Isaac wealthy. Why? Because when God decides to bless you, your environment cannot stop it. Your economy cannot limit it. Your circumstances cannot prevent it. Your enemies cannot block it. The blessing of God transcends natural systems. It overrides earthly limitations. It defies logical projections. It laughs at statistical models. And I decree over your life today, even in the farming of this season, even in the drought of this economy, even in the scarcity of these times, you will be blessed, not a little, a hundredfold. But it never ran out, it kept coming, it kept multiplying, it kept providing. Now, here is the point. The widow became an unexpected blessing to Elijah, and because she became an unexpected blessing, she received an unexpected miracle. The blessing she gave out of nowhere triggered a miracle she could not have manufactured on her own. This is the divine economy. When you become a blessing, you trigger blessings. When you give unexpectedly, you receive unexpectedly. When you sow from your last, God multiplies your future. And when someone blesses you out of nowhere, it is not random, it is God using their generosity to position you for multiplication. So, I want you to hear me clearly today.
